The report by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) examines grant programs awarded by the Departments of Health and Human Services (HHS), Labor (DOL), and Justice (DOJ) from 2007 to 2015 that were subject to statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring. The report identified 2,586 grantees who received funding through at least 53 grant programs, with 19 potential Faith-Based Organizations (FBOs) among them.

HHS identified one grant program, the Projects for Assistance in Transition from Homelessness (PATH), which was subject to statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring, but no grants were awarded to nonprofit organizations, and therefore no FBOs received funding.

DOL identified 18 grant programs in its Employment and Training Administration (ETA) that were subject to statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring, and 19 FBOs were identified among the 911 grantees.

DOJ identified at least 34 grant programs across various offices that were subject to statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring, but the number could be higher. Of these, nine FBOs certified that they were exempt from the restrictions and received funding.

The report also discusses the methods used by the agencies to inform grant applicants and recipients of the statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring, including grant announcements and web pages.

The report concludes that while the agencies require grantees to self-certify their eligibility for exemptions from statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring, only a small number of FBOs have sought and received exemptions. The report also notes that some FBOs interviewed stated that hiring individuals of the same faith was critical to their mission and organizational success.

The report was provided to the Departments of Labor, Justice, and Health and Human Services for technical comments, and will be distributed to appropriate congressional committees and made available on the GAO website 30 days after the report date.
